whatItIs.heading: What is fire damage restoration?
whatItIs.body: Fire damage restoration is the full-cycle process of returning a home to its pre-loss condition after a structure fire, kitchen fire, or electrical fire. It begins before the smoke clears and does not end until the structure is rebuilt. The scope covers emergency board-up and tarping to secure the property, removal of charred materials and fire-damaged structural components, smoke and soot cleaning across every surface the fire touched, water damage remediation caused by firefighting suppression, odor elimination using thermal fogging and hydroxyl treatment, HVAC decontamination, content restoration for salvageable belongings, and final reconstruction. Fire damage is not a single problem—it is four overlapping problems: burn damage, smoke penetration, suppression water, and persistent odor. Resolving all four requires a coordinated crew, not a sequence of separate contractors.

process.heading: How Gallagher handles fire damage restoration

steps.title: Emergency stabilization and assessment
steps.body: Gallagher Restoration Co. arrives on-site, typically within 60 minutes. The crew boards up breached windows and doors, applies roof tarps where needed, documents structural damage with photos, and performs a full walk-through before any materials are moved. Nothing is discarded without documentation.

steps.title: Demolition and water mitigation
steps.body: Charred framing, fire-damaged drywall, and saturated materials from firefighting suppression are removed and documented for the insurance claim. Water left by hoses and sprinklers is extracted and the affected structure is set up for drying—a step most homeowners do not anticipate but every fire job requires.

steps.title: Smoke, soot, and odor treatment
steps.body: IICRC-trained technicians clean smoke residue from framing, ceilings, walls, and contents using methods matched to the residue type—dry sponge for dry smoke, wet chemical cleaners for wet smoke, enzyme treatment for protein residue. Thermal fogging and hydroxyl generators address embedded odor in porous materials.

steps.title: Reconstruction and final walkthrough
steps.body: The same Gallagher crew rebuilds—replacing drywall, flooring, cabinetry, insulation, and paint. No subcontractor handoff, no scheduling gap between mitigation and rebuild. The job closes with a final air quality check and a walkthrough with the homeowner.

signs.heading: Signs you need fire damage restoration—even after a small fire
signs.intro: The visible char is only one layer of the problem. Smoke, soot, and suppression water travel far beyond the area that burned.

items.title: Any structure fire, regardless of size
items.body: A contained kitchen fire or an electrical fire in one room still sends smoke through wall gaps, HVAC ducts, and ceiling cavities. What looks limited rarely is.

items.title: Persistent smoke odor after ventilation
items.body: If the smell returns after opening windows, smoke residue has penetrated porous materials—insulation, drywall, flooring, upholstery—and will not resolve without professional treatment.

items.title: Soot or black residue on walls and ceilings
items.body: Soot is corrosive. Left on surfaces, it etches paint, stains drywall paper, and permanently discolors ceilings. The window for cleaning without full replacement shortens by the hour.

items.title: Water-stained or buckled materials from suppression
items.body: Firefighting hoses and sprinklers deliver significant water. Saturated insulation, flooring, and wall cavities set up the same mold risk as a plumbing flood if not extracted and dried promptly.

items.title: Charred or heat-compromised structural components
items.body: Framing, joists, and sheathing exposed to fire can lose structural integrity even without full combustion. A visual inspection alone cannot determine load capacity—professional assessment is required before re-occupancy.

whyUs.heading: Why homeowners call Gallagher for fire damage restoration
whyUs.body:
Gallagher Restoration Co. has managed fire damage jobs across Southern California for more than 15 years—structure fires, kitchen fires, electrical fires, and wildfire-adjacent smoke events. The work is complicated because it stacks four distinct damage types on top of each other. Crews that handle only one—say, soot cleaning but not water mitigation—leave the homeowner to coordinate the rest. That coordination gap is where claims get delayed, mold colonizes the suppression water, and odor comes back six months later.

Gallagher is built as a single-crew solution. IICRC-trained technicians handle emergency stabilization, smoke and soot remediation, suppression water extraction, odor treatment, and full reconstruction without handing off to a separate contractor. The crew documents every affected item and every structural measurement for the insurance claim file from day one. When you call (951) 541-0034, a real person answers and a crew is typically on-site within 60 minutes anywhere in the Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange, San Diego, or Los Angeles county footprint.

pricing.heading: Fire damage restoration pricing—what to expect
pricing.body: Every job starts with a free on-site assessment; there is no charge to show up, document, and scope the work. Fire damage restoration in Southern California typically ranges from $3,000 to $75,000 or more. The lower end covers a contained kitchen or small room fire where the structure is intact and the primary work is soot cleaning, odor treatment, and cosmetic repair. The upper end reflects a major structural fire requiring full demolition of fire-damaged sections, suppression water remediation, and complete interior reconstruction. Scope, the extent of smoke penetration, the volume of suppression water, and structural involvement all drive the final number. Gallagher Restoration Co. coordinates directly with your insurance carrier and builds the documentation package the adjuster needs from day one.

faqs.q: How long does fire damage restoration take?
faqs.a: A contained fire with soot and odor as the primary issues typically takes one to two weeks. Jobs involving structural fire damage, significant suppression water, and full reconstruction run four to twelve weeks depending on scope and permit timelines. Gallagher Restoration Co. provides a written scope and timeline during the initial assessment.

faqs.q: Does homeowners insurance cover fire damage restoration in California?
faqs.a: Standard homeowners policies in California cover fire damage restoration, including the cost of smoke cleanup, water damage from suppression, and structural rebuild. Coverage limits, deductibles, and specific exclusions vary by policy. Gallagher Restoration Co. documents cause, scope, and affected materials from day one and coordinates directly with your adjuster throughout the claim.

faqs.q: Can I stay in my home during fire damage restoration?
faqs.a: It depends on what burned and how far smoke penetrated. A small, well-contained fire in one room may allow occupancy elsewhere in the home while work proceeds. Fires involving structural damage, compromised electrical systems, or widespread smoke infiltration through the HVAC typically require temporary relocation until the structure is cleared.

faqs.q: What is the difference between fire damage restoration and smoke clean-up?
faqs.a: Smoke clean-up is a sub-service that addresses soot, smoke residue, and odor in properties where the structure is intact—common after a neighbor's fire or a contained kitchen incident. Fire damage restoration is the full-cycle process that also includes demolition of burned materials, suppression water mitigation, and structural reconstruction. Many jobs involve both.

faqs.q: What should I do immediately after a fire in my home?
faqs.a: Ensure everyone's safety first and call 911 if you haven't already. Once the fire department has secured the scene, contact your insurance company to report the loss. Do not re-enter the damaged area until authorities have declared it structurally safe, and do not attempt to power on electrical systems in affected zones.

faqs.q: Is it safe to re-enter my home after a fire?
faqs.a: Only after the fire department declares it safe. Even then, be cautious of structural damage, compromised electrical systems, lingering smoke and toxic residue, and slip hazards from suppression water. When in doubt, wait for a professional restoration assessment before spending extended time inside.

faqs.q: How can I assess the extent of the fire damage?
faqs.a: Hire a professional fire damage restoration company to assess the property thoroughly. Fire damage stacks four separate problems—burn damage, smoke penetration, suppression water, and embedded odor—and a full assessment includes structural inspection, moisture mapping, smoke residue classification, and HVAC evaluation. Gallagher provides that assessment at no cost.

faqs.q: What should I document for insurance purposes?
faqs.a: Photograph or video every damaged item and every affected structural area before anything is moved or discarded. Keep a written log of all communication with your insurance carrier, adjuster, and contractors. Save receipts for temporary lodging and emergency purchases. Gallagher Restoration Co. builds and shares that documentation package for you from day one on the job.

faqs.q: Can I salvage any of my belongings after a fire?
faqs.a: Many items can be salvaged, but it depends on residue type, heat exposure, and how quickly restoration begins. Textiles, electronics, documents, and photos often respond to professional content restoration. Porous items with deep smoke penetration or heat damage may need to be replaced. A restoration professional inventories and evaluates every item before decisions are made.

faqs.q: How can I prevent future fires in my home?
faqs.a: Install working smoke detectors on every floor and carbon monoxide detectors near sleeping areas. Maintain heating systems, chimneys, dryer vents, and electrical panels on a regular schedule. Create and practice a fire escape plan with your family, and keep a working fire extinguisher in the kitchen and garage.

faqs.q: How can I ensure the safety of my home after restoration?
faqs.a: Follow the recommendations from your fire restoration team, including any air-quality clearance results and electrical or structural sign-offs. Keep up with routine maintenance on HVAC, smoke detectors, and electrical systems, and address any small issues promptly so they don't compound into another loss.

faqs.q: What can I do to emotionally cope with the aftermath of a house fire?
faqs.a: Seek support from friends, family, or professionals. A house fire is a traumatic event, and it is common for the emotional impact to surface days or weeks after the physical damage is addressed. Counseling or therapy can help you and your family process the loss and re-establish a sense of normal.

faqs.q: How do I find a reputable fire damage restoration company?
faqs.a: Ask your insurance provider, friends, or family for recommendations. Check online reviews and verify the company's credentials, licenses, and IICRC training. Look for a crew that handles the full lifecycle—stabilization through reconstruction—so you're not managing handoffs between separate contractors while you're already displaced.
